lead.en: Dusit is Bangkok at its most formal: the Dusit Palace complex, the Marble Temple, Government House, and since August 2019 the Sappaya-Sapasathan parliament on the Kiakkai riverfront - 424,000 square metres, the world's largest parliament building. It is also the quietest khet in this researched comparison set (about 7,100 residents per km2) and, unusually for inner Bangkok, one with no BTS or MRT station inside it - buses and river piers carry the commute until the MRT Purple extension opens (2030 target, four planned stations). Green coverage looks abundant (10.5%) but much of it is royal or institutional ground; the old zoo has been fenced since 2018 with its replacement built far out in Pathum Thani. Rents run 9k-28k for listed stock. The trade-offs are as formal as the district: thin nightlife, thin retail, and a September 2025 tunnel-construction sinkhole that closed Samsen Road.

strengths.en: Quiet at inner-Bangkok density: 7,109/km2, the researched comparison set's lowest, across palace grounds, ministries and university campuses - a genuinely calm address.
Rents under-index the postcode: listed 1BRs from 9k-13k THB and 2BRs 20k-28k (Oct 2026), with only a thin 25-listing market - value before the 2030 metro arrives.

tradeoffs.en: Transit-poor by design, not accident: no BTS/MRT station inside the khet; rail stops sit on its edges (Yommarat, Sam Sen, the non-public Chitrlada halt) until MRT Purple's Nov-2030 target.

The 10.5% park share is not walkable-to green: the zoo chunk has been fenced since 2018, Sanam Suea Pa is a royal-household office site, and Suan Chitlada is a residence quarter - public usable parkland is far smaller than the number implies.

dayNight.en: Days follow ministries, parliament sessions and hospital shifts; after dark the district effectively closes - no nightlife venue type appeared in any source read, and riverside Kiakkai is a parliament corner, not a promenade scene.

fit.en: Strong fit for people whose life is the state itself - parliament, ministries, camps, hospitals - and for quiet-seekers who accept bus-and-boat transit until 2030.
Avoid if you need rail at the door or a functioning Samsen frontage today: the sinkhole closure and the 2030 metro horizon define daily logistics for now.
